C0.quote: We model an election in which voters can reelect an incumbent
C0.note: The object is a two-candidate election (partisans plus a representative independent voter) and the strategic signalling of the incumbent before it. This is a strategic aspect of a voting procedure.

C1.quote: two polar pure strategy Perfect Bayesian Equilibria (PBE) exist
C1.note: The main results are existence conditions for separating, pooling and mixed PBE (EQ). The social welfare comparisons in Sect. 5 are WD.

C2.1.value: votes / independent vote (voting for the incumbent or the opponent)
C2.1.quote: An independent voter thus votes for the incumbent (v(d) = 1)

C2.2.quote: the independent voter’s strategy (probability of voting for the incumbent)
C2.2.note: Binary vote between incumbent and opponent; partisans always vote for their preferred candidate.

C2.3.quote: The utility of the independent voter is the expected welfare generated
C2.3.note: Voters hold utilities, beliefs about ability and a conformity bonus W; partisans have a preferred candidate.

C2.4.quote: This is not the case when voters are conformists.
C2.4.note: The vote v(d) is a choice, separate from utility and beliefs. With conformism the vote can depart from the candidate with the highest expected ability.

C3.1.quote: the voting decisions that maximize the voter’s utility given beliefs updating
C3.1.note: In all analyses the independent voter chooses his vote to maximise utility including the conformity bonus, so the vote may differ from his ability-based preference. Partisans are passive.

C4.1.note: The input format is OTH (binary vote), not one of the listed formats.

C5.1.quote: social welfare is the sum of the expected benefits created

C5.2.quote: social welfare is the sum of the expected benefits created by the elected politician
C5.2.note: Welfare is evaluated on policy benefits and abilities, not on votes.

VOT.quote_behav: An independent voter thus votes for the incumbent (v(d) = 1)
VOT.quote_info: he does not know the size of the incumbent’s partisan support
VOT.note: The representative independent voter is strategic. Partisans are passive: 'partisans who always vote for their preferred candidate'. The independent voter observes d and μo.

CAN.quote_behav: she may want to distort her choice before running
CAN.quote_info: It is unknown to the incumbent at the time she takes decision d.
CAN.note: The incumbent chooses policy d strategically. She knows the voters' strategy rule but not μo. The opponent takes no action.

C7.1.quote: While partisans are passive players by definition
C7.1.note: The present types VOT and CAN are both strategic. The strategic/passive split (independent voter vs. partisans) lies within the VOT type.

C8.1.note: Perfect Bayesian Equilibrium of a signalling game, refined by the Intuitive Criterion.
